newsitem.title: UK: UK Foinaven oil start now seen Q1 97 after delays.
newsitem.headline: UK Foinaven oil start now seen Q1 97 after delays.

text.p: The start of production from the U.K. Foinaven oilfield in Atlantic waters is now confirmed for first quarter 1997 after an engineering problem has been resolved, a spokesman for operator British Petroleum Co Plc said.
Foinaven, the first field to be developed in Atlantic waters west of the Shetland Islands, was originally scheduled to come on stream in June.
But BP ordered an investigation into a faulty subsea manifold after the discovery in May of hairline cracks and said first oil would be delayed into the fourth quarter.
The BP spokesman said a new manifold and the shuttle tanker needed for production will reach the field in October.
He said the main problem with the manifold was one of engineering that was the result of "overactive stress" during the manufacture of the manifold.
"We discovered after eight or nine weeks of close investigation that the problem was one of stress and embrittlement which we suspected all along," he added.
Production in the first stage of Foinaven is expected to run at 85,000 barrels per day. -- Karen Matusic, London newsroom, +44 171 542 6280
